issues.location: Products with 50+ reviews convert at 2-3x compared to products with no reviews (Bazaarvoice / Spiegel).
issues.explanation: The Spiegel Research Center finding is that 5 reviews yield a 270% conversion uplift vs. zero reviews — not '50+ reviews at 2-3x'. The '50+ reviews' threshold and '2-3x' multiplier are a distorted version of the original stat and should not be attributed to Bazaarvoice/Spiegel.

issues.location: Product recommendations drive 10-30% of e-commerce revenue (McKinsey)
issues.explanation: This is a debunked benchmark. McKinsey never published a finding that product recommendations drive 10-30% of e-commerce revenue. This stat is widely circulated but has no verified McKinsey source.

issues.location: the average AOV uplift with cross-sell is 8-15% (Baymard Institute)
issues.explanation: Baymard Institute has not published research finding an 8-15% AOV uplift from cross-sell. This is a fabricated attribution to a real research organization.

issues.location: Unique product descriptions are associated with meaningful organic traffic improvements per PDP (industry estimates suggest 30–50%, though results vary by category and competition).
issues.explanation: The claim that unique descriptions increase traffic by 30-50% is a debunked benchmark never published by Ahrefs or any verified source. Even without a named attribution here, flagging this as a fabricated industry figure is warranted given it matches the known debunked stat.

issues.location: A screenshot of the Bash.com PDP (The FIX Trench Coat) could not be independently verified — the page may have been behind a WAF or bot-protection layer (common on VTEX IO PDPs), and the capture cannot be confirmed to reflect live site content.
issues.explanation: The report acknowledges that a PDP screenshot may show a WAF/bot-protection page rather than real site content, yet the screenshot is still referenced in the report without being clearly excluded or flagged as invalid. Screenshots from WAF-intercepted responses should not be presented as evidence of live site content.

summary: The report contains three fabricated benchmarks (Spiegel '50+ reviews', McKinsey '10-30% revenue from recommendations', Baymard '8-15% AOV uplift'), a likely debunked '30-50%' unique description traffic claim, and a WAF screenshot disclosure that is insufficiently handled; all other checks pass cleanly.

edits.original: Products with 50+ reviews convert at 2-3x compared to products with no reviews (Bazaarvoice / Spiegel).
edits.fixed: Products with 5 or more reviews see a 270% higher purchase likelihood compared to products with no reviews (Spiegel Research Center, 2017).
edits.rationale: The correct Spiegel Research Center stat is that 5+ reviews yield a 270% conversion uplift vs. zero reviews. The '50+ reviews at 2-3x' version is a distortion of the original finding.

edits.original: Product recommendations drive 10-30% of e-commerce revenue (McKinsey), and the average AOV uplift with cross-sell is 8-15% (Baymard Institute).
edits.fixed: Personalization — of which product recommendations are a core component — drives a 5–15% revenue lift (McKinsey, 2021).
edits.rationale: McKinsey's verified stat is that personalization drives 5–15% revenue lift, not that recommendations drive 10–30% of revenue. The Baymard '8–15% AOV' claim has no verified source and has been removed entirely per guidelines.

edits.rationale: The 30–50% figure matches a known fabricated benchmark with no verified source. The specific percentage has been removed and the claim softened to reflect genuine uncertainty.

edits.fixed: A screenshot of the Bash.com PDP (The FIX Trench Coat) was not captured — the page was behind a WAF or bot-protection layer (common on VTEX IO PDPs) and the screenshot therefore cannot be used as evidence of live site content.
